mainTopic: The verse of the שבעת המינים (as measurements and as the order of ברכות), and which ברכות are needed for foods eaten during or after a bread meal
overview: The גמרא finishes reading the verse of the שבעת המינים as a hint to halachic measurements. רמון is the hole that ends a vessel's status, זית shows that most measurements are a כזית, and דבש is the large date of יום הכפורים. It then explains that these measurements are only מדרבנן and the verse is just an אסמכתא, so the verse can still teach the order of ברכות. In a story, רב המנונא blesses dates before pomegranates. רב חסדא challenges him, and רב המנונא answers that the order is counted from the nearest word 'ארץ'. Next, אמוראים argue about fruit eaten during a bread meal: does it need a ברכה before, after, or both? רב פפא gives the final הלכה in three cases, depending on whether the food is part of the meal and when it is eaten. Finally, בן זומא explains that bread exempts the meal-foods. The גמרא asks why bread does not exempt wine, and the answer, 'wine is different,' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The pomegranate hints at the measure for a broken vessel
steps.stepSummary: The word רמון in the verse hints that a householder's vessel loses its status as a כלי, and its טומאה, once it has a hole the size of a pomegranate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their measure is the size of pomegranates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the line about רמון from the list that began on the previous amud. Each fruit in the verse hints at a halachic measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this point, the גמרא matched חטה, שעורה, גפן and תאנה to different measurements. Here רמון is matched to the rule about כלי בעלי בתים, the vessels of ordinary householders. Such a vessel stops counting as a כלי, and so becomes טהור, only when its hole is as big as a pomegranate.

keyTerms.meaning: A halachic measurement or minimum amount
Vessels of ordinary householders (the case behind this line)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that began earlier on the דף. The subject is the vessels of householders, which only lose their טומאה when the hole is pomegranate-sized.

phrases.english: Their measure is the size of pomegranates.
phrases.notes: Refers to the hole that makes a householder's vessel no longer count as a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of measurements on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רמון in the verse hints at the pomegranate-sized hole that ends a householder's vessel's status as a כלי.

steps.title: The olive hints that the land's measures are olive-sized
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'ארץ זית שמן' as 'a land whose measures are all the size of olives.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A land of olive oil': רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said, a land all of whose measures are the size of olives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא explains the word זית in the verse. He says it hints that the measurements of ארץ ישראל's laws are כזית, the size of an olive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many halachos use the size of an olive, called a כזית, as their measurement. Examples are eating forbidden foods and eating מצה. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא first says this is true of ALL the measurements, and that wording is what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an olive, the most common halachic measurement

phrases.english: 'A land of olive oil'
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
A land all of whose measures are the size of olives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ זֵית שֶׁמֶן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next food in the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זית hints that the land's measurements are olive-sized.

steps.title: Challenge: not all measures are olive-sized
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we just listed many measurements that are not olive-sized, such as barley, figs and pomegranates.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it enter your mind that ALL its measures are olive-sized? But there are those measures we just mentioned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the word 'all' (כל) in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same verse was just used to teach other sizes, such as a barley grain, a dried fig and a pomegranate. So it cannot be true that every measurement is a כזית. The attack is aimed only at the word 'all', not at the whole idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (a phrase that rejects an idea)

phrases.english: Can it enter your mind that it means ALL its measures?!
But there are those measures that we mentioned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'all' (כל) in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse itself was just used to teach measurements that are not olive-sized, so 'all' is impossible.

steps.title: Answer: most measures are olive-sized
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the verse means 'a land where MOST of the measures are olive-sized.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: a land most of whose measures are the size of olives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the statement by changing 'all' to 'most'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic idea stays the same: the olive hints at a measurement. Only the claim is narrowed. Most halachic measurements, such as forbidden foods and טומאה of a dead body, are a כזית, while the few exceptions are the sizes listed earlier.

phrases.english: Rather: a land most of whose measures are the size of olives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3.

steps.title: Date-honey hints at the יום הכפורים measure
steps.stepSummary: דבש (date honey) hints that the measure for eating on יום הכפורים is the size of a large date.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Honey': the size of a large date, for יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last food in the verse, דבש. It refers to dates, and dates hint at the יום הכפורים measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'honey' in this verse is date honey, so the hint is to the date itself. A person is only liable for eating on יום הכפורים if he eats as much as a כותבת הגסה, a large date. This is a bigger amount than a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Honey (here: date honey, so it means dates)
The size of a large date
The Day of Atonement, when eating is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, every food in the verse hints at a halachic measurement. רמון is the vessel's hole, זית is most measurements, and דבש is the large date of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: 'Honey' (i.e., dates)
The size of a large date, on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דבש hints at the large-date measure for eating on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: What does the other opinion do with this reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the other אמורא, who uses the verse for the order of ברכות, deals with the measurements reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: This one-word question sets up the next move. The גמרא asks how the opposing view deals with the verse being used for measurements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, another אמורא used this same verse to teach which food gets its ברכה first. If the verse is busy teaching measurements, how can he also use it for ברכות? Or, in the other direction, how does he answer this reading?

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (what does the other opinion say?)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אידך' means the OTHER אמורא, the one who reads the verse as teaching the order of ברכות. It does not mean another measurement.

phrases.english: And the other (Amora, how does he deal with this)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the measurements reading back to the opposing opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the opinion that the verse teaches the order of ברכות responds to the measurements reading.

steps.title: The measures are rabbinic; the verse is only a hint
steps.stepSummary: The measurements are not written explicitly in the תורה. They are מדרבנן, and the verse is only an אסמכתא. So the verse is still free to teach the order of ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these measures written explicitly in the תורה? Rather, they are rabbinic, and the verse is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the measurements reading is not a true explanation of the verse. It is just a hint for rules set by the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the measurements are מדרבנן, the verse is not really 'used up' by them. It is only an אסמכתא, a memory hook. That leaves the verse's real meaning open, so the other אמורא can learn the order of ברכות from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A mere support / hint (not the true source of the law)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key general idea. A verse can be an אסמכתא for rabbinic laws while its true meaning is used for something else.

phrases.english: Are these measures written explicitly?
Rather, they are rabbinic,
and the verse is a mere support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measurements are מדרבנן and the verse is only an אסמכתא, so the verse's real meaning (the order of ברכות) still stands.

steps.title: Story: רב המנונא blesses dates before pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: At a meal, dates and pomegranates were served. רב המנונא made his ברכה on the dates first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב המנונא were sitting at a meal. Dates and pomegranates were brought before them. רב המנונא took some and blessed on the dates first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about the order of ברכות. It sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both foods are from the שבעת המינים: dates are the 'דבש' of the verse, and pomegranates are 'רמון'. רב המנונא chose to bless the dates first, even though pomegranates appear earlier in the verse.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוֹדְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna were sitting at a meal.
They brought before them dates and pomegranates.
Rav Hamnuna took,
and blessed on the dates first.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוֹדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a practical story about the order of ברכות, the reading that the previous step showed still stands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב המנונא blessed on dates before pomegranates.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges: the verse's order decides
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב המנונא whether he doesn't hold the rule that whatever comes earlier in this verse gets its ברכה first. Pomegranates come before dates in the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Doesn't the Master hold the teaching of רב יוסף, and some say רבי יצחק: whatever comes earlier in this verse comes first for a blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges רב המנונא's order. He cites the rule that the verse's order decides which food is blessed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists רמון before דבש (dates). So by the rule of רב יוסף (or רבי יצחק), pomegranates should have been blessed first. The question is worded like a question, but it works as a challenge to רב המנונא's action.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master hold (a polite challenge)
And some say (another name for the same teaching)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule of קדימה בברכות: among the שבעת המינים, the order of the verse decides which food is blessed first.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him:
Does the Master not hold

phrases.aramaic: לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: this that Rav Yosef said, and some say Rabbi Yitzḥak:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמּוּקְדָּם בְּפָסוּק זֶה קוֹדֵם לִבְרָכָה?
phrases.english: Whatever comes earlier in this verse comes first for a blessing?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's action in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's choice to bless dates before pomegranates
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse lists רמון before דבש (dates), and the rule says the verse's order sets the order of ברכות.

steps.title: רב המנונא counts from the word 'ארץ'
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers רב חסדא: dates are second after the word 'ארץ', and pomegranates are only fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one (the date) is second to the word 'land,' and this one (the pomegranate) is fifth to the word 'land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers רב חסדא's challenge. He says that when you count from the word 'ארץ', dates actually come before pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'ארץ' twice. The first time is 'ארץ חטה ושערה וגפן ותאנה ורמון', and the second time is 'ארץ זית שמן ודבש'. Counting from the closest 'ארץ', דבש (dates) is second. Pomegranate is fifth from the first 'ארץ'. So the closer a food is to a word 'ארץ', the earlier its ברכה, and the date wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Honey; here it means date honey, so it stands for dates

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count straight through the whole verse. The count starts over at each word 'ארץ'.

phrases.english: He said to him: This one is second to 'land,'
phrases.notes: He means the date (דבש): in 'ארץ זית שמן ודבש' it's the second item after 'land.'

phrases.english: and this one is fifth to 'land.'
phrases.notes: He means the pomegranate, which comes fifth after 'land' in the first list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting how the verse's order is measured
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pomegranates come earlier in the verse, so they should get their ברכה first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is measured by distance from the nearest word 'ארץ', so dates come first.

steps.title: רב חסדא praises רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא accepts the answer and praises רב המנונא's sharpness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who will give us iron legs, so that we can serve you and hear Torah from you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא is impressed by the answer and praises רב המנונא. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise shows that רב חסדא fully accepts the answer. He wishes he had tireless 'iron legs' so he could always follow רב המנונא and learn from him.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who will give us
iron legs, and we will serve you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב המנונא's explanation stands: dates come before pomegranates for the order of ברכות.

steps.title: רב הונא: fruit during a meal needs a ברכה only before
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: figs and grapes brought during a meal. רב הונא says they need a ברכה before eating them, but no ברכה after.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If they brought figs and grapes before them during the meal, רב הונא said: They need a blessing before eating them, and they do not need a blessing after eating them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: fruit served in the middle of a meal with bread. רב הונא gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit is not part of the bread meal, so the המוציא on the bread does not cover it, and it needs its own ברכה first. But ברכת המזון at the end does cover it, so no separate ברכה is said afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
They need a blessing before eating them

phrases.english: It was stated: If they brought before them
figs and grapes during the meal,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: טְעוּנִים בְּרָכָה לִפְנֵיהֶם
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: They require a blessing before them
and do not require a blessing after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הֵבִיאוּ לִפְנֵיהֶם תְּאֵנִים וַעֲנָבִים בְּתוֹךְ הַסְּעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, unrelated to the order of ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit eaten during a meal needs a ברכה before it, but not after it.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds the same ruling as רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רב נחמן said: They need a blessing before eating them, and they do not need a blessing after eating them.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב נחמן, agrees with רב הונא. This adds weight to his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule itself. The point is that this opinion is held by two major אמוראים.

phrases.english: And so too Rav Nachman said:
They require a blessing before them
and do not require a blessing after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same as רב הונא: a ברכה before, but not after.

steps.title: רב ששת: a ברכה both before and after
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds that the fruit needs a ברכה both before and after. The only exception is פת הבאה בכסנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: They need a blessing both before and after eating them. For there is nothing that needs a blessing before it but not after it, except for פת הבאה בכסנין (sweet pastry) alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת disagrees with רב הונא and רב נחמן. He gives a general rule to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת holds that ברכת המזון does not cover the fruit. So the fruit needs its own ברכה afterward too. His general rule is: if a food needs its own ברכה before, it also needs its own ברכה after. The one exception is פת הבאה בכסנין, because it is a kind of bread, so ברכת המזון does cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sweet or spiced pastry, a type of bread

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: טְעוּנִין בְּרָכָה בֵּין לִפְנֵיהֶם בֵּין לְאַחֲרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: They require a blessing both before them and after them.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁטָּעוּן בְּרָכָה לְפָנָיו
phrases.english: For you have nothing that requires a blessing before it
and does not require a blessing after it
except sweet pastry-bread alone.
phrases.notes: It is a kind of bread, so ברכת המזון covers it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes steps 12 and 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit during a meal needs a ברכה both before and after.

steps.title: Both views disagree with רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that both opinions argue with רבי חייא, who holds that bread exempts all foods and wine exempts all drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי חייא, for רבי חייא said: Bread exempts all kinds of food, and wine exempts all kinds of drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a third view exists: רבי חייא's. Both earlier opinions disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי חייא, the bread covers the fruit completely, so no ברכה is needed before or after. That conflicts with רב הונא, who requires a ברכה before. It also conflicts with רב ששת, who requires a ברכה before and after.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Chiya
for Rabbi Chiya said:
Bread exempts all kinds of food,
and wine exempts all kinds of drinks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places both opinions against a third opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא: bread exempts all foods, and wine exempts all drinks.

steps.title: רב פפא's final הלכה: three cases
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules in three cases: meal-foods during the meal need no ברכה; other foods during the meal need a ברכה only before; foods after the meal need a ברכה before and after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is: Foods that come because of the meal, eaten during the meal, need no blessing, neither before nor after. Foods that do not come because of the meal, eaten during the meal, need a blessing before but not after. Foods eaten after the meal need a blessing both before and after.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the dispute with the final הלכה. He splits it into three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foods that are part of the meal (like meat and fish eaten with bread) are covered fully by the bread. Fruit eaten during the meal needs its own ברכה first, but ברכת המזון covers it afterward, like רב הונא. Food eaten after the meal is finished is a separate eating, so it needs a ברכה both before and after.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the meal (part of the meal itself)
Not because of the meal (like fruit or dessert)

steps.whatToRemember: Three cases: (1) Meal-foods during the meal need no ברכה. (2) Non-meal foods during the meal need a ברכה only before. (3) Foods after the meal need a ברכה before and after.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מחמת הסעודה' is about what kind of food it is (part of the meal or not). It is not about when it is eaten. Timing is a separate question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for ברכות during a bread meal.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The halacha is
items that come because of the meal
during the meal —
do not require a blessing
neither before them nor after them.
And those not because of the meal, during the meal —
require a blessing before them
and do not require a blessing after them.
After the meal —

phrases.aramaic: טְעוּנִים בְּרָכָה בֵּין לִפְנֵיהֶם בֵּין לְאַחֲרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: they require a blessing both before them and after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute of steps 12 to 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברכה depends on whether the food is part of the meal and on whether it is eaten during or after the meal.

steps.title: בן זומא is asked why meal-foods need no ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The students ask בן זומא why foods that are part of the meal need no ברכה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked בן זומא: Why did they say that foods that come because of the meal, eaten during the meal, need no blessing, neither before nor after?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a question that was put to בן זומא. They want to know the reason behind the first rule. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is already known. The question is only asking for its reason.

phrases.english: They asked Ben Zoma:
Why did they say

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים הַבָּאִים מֵחֲמַת הַסְּעוּדָה בְּתוֹךְ הַסְּעוּדָה
phrases.english: that items coming because of the meal, during the meal,
do not require a blessing
neither before them nor after them?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת בֶּן זוֹמָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first case of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason that meal-foods are exempt from a ברכה.

steps.title: Because the bread exempts them
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא answers that the bread exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Because the bread exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא gives the reason: the bread is the main food, and its ברכה covers the foods eaten with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meal-foods are secondary to the bread. So the המוציא before and the ברכת המזון after cover them too.

phrases.english: He said to them: Because bread exempts them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bread exempts the foods that are part of the meal.

steps.title: Then bread should exempt wine too
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: if bread exempts meal-foods, it should exempt wine as well. Yet wine gets its own ברכה during a meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the bread should also exempt wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בן זומא's reason. Wine drunk during a meal still needs its own ברכה, so why doesn't the bread cover it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bread covers everything that comes with the meal, wine should be included. But in practice we make a separate בורא פרי הגפן on wine during a meal. That seems to contradict the reason.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, יַיִן נָמֵי נִפְטְרֵיהּ פַּת!
phrases.english: If so, let bread also exempt wine!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, יַיִן נָמֵי נִפְטְרֵיהּ פַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן זומא's reason that bread exempts the foods of the meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine also comes with the meal, yet it gets its own ברכה. So the reason seems inconsistent.

steps.title: Wine is different
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: wine is different. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine is different...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer: wine is a special case. This line is setting up the explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that bread exempts meal-foods still stands. Wine is treated as an exception for its own reason, which the גמרא is about to give.

phrases.english: Wine is different
phrases.notes: The reason continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bread should exempt wine like any other meal-food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine is a special case (the explanation follows on the next amud).
